description: Prompt-time routing table for the bench UserPromptSubmit hook. Each route that matches contributes one directive injected alongside the user's prompt. Patterns are JS regex source, matched case-insensitively.

unless: \b(explain|what does|what is|how does|why does|show me|glance|sanity.?check|remind me|status of|link to|task list|todo list|backlog|the board)\b
routes.message: This prompt reads as starting work on a task ({{issues}}). Invoke the bench:task-start skill BEFORE any file edit — it resolves the base branch, checks for an existing branch locally and on origin, creates or switches to it, and runs worktree init. Branch shape comes from bench:git-conventions: <type>/<issue-number>_<short-goal>. Do not create the branch by hand and do not edit files first.

when: \b(ship it|we'?re done|close (this|the) task|wrap (this|it) up|finish (this|the) task|open (a|the) PR|create (a|the) PR|raise (a|the) PR)\b
routes.message: This is task wrap-up. Invoke the bench:task-completion skill — it runs the tests, opens the PR as draft with the type and size labels the pr-labels rule requires, waits for your OK before publishing, announces on Discord or GitHub Discussions, then closes the issue on merge. Do not open the PR directly.

Per the pr-review-via-agent rule: delegate to the bench:code-reviewer agent. It pulls the PR, picks the language checklist (review-javascript / review-dotnet / review-sql), produces the severity-graded findings, and posts inline plus summary comments. State whether the PR is standalone or part of an integration bundle — without that context the agent flags planned gaps as criticals. Do not review ad-hoc in chat. Respect pr-comment-action-scope for change-requesting comments.

unless: \b(don'?t create|no ticket|no issue|without a ticket|without an issue|skip the ticket|skip the issue)\b
routes.message: Issue authoring goes through the bench:scrum-master agent (or bench:business-analyst when starting from a PRD). It resolves owner/repo through bench:github-context, then follows the bench:github-issues skill for labels, size estimate and body shape. Use the gh CLI — do not hand-roll the REST call.

unless: \b(run the tests|tests are failing|why (is|are) (the )?tests?|fix the test)\b
routes.message: Test authoring goes to the bench:qa-automation agent, which follows bench:testing-conventions — integration over unit for routes and repos, real infrastructure over mocks, no logger stubs, only external services stubbed. Tests must be able to actually fail.

bench:testing-conventions is explicit that a failing test is real until proven otherwise. Before calling anything flaky: reproduce the exact spec locally, re-run for determinism, compare against the base branch, and name the actual mechanism. Re-queueing CI to get green without a root cause hides a regression.

This is solution-architect territory (service boundaries, schema and caching design). Delegate to the bench:solution-architect agent rather than designing inline. It stays advisory — design and diagrams, then hand implementation to senior-developer and test design to qa-automation.

prior-art-first applies: before drafting a new helper, grep the *concept* (field / path / operation being resolved) across sibling handlers, common/ and helpers/ folders, and the largest file in the area. Try two or three keyword variations before concluding there is no prior art. Lift the existing pattern rather than converging on a worse API.

when: \b(plan (this|it|the)|make a plan|design (an|the) approach|how should we approach)\b
unless: \b(no plan|skip the plan|just do it|don'?t plan)\b
routes.message: Invoke the bench:plan-workflow skill for structured planning and alignment before implementation. Scale the Phase 3 coverage review to the risk — a small, well-understood change does not need three specialist agents.

Posting to Discord or GitHub Discussions: follow the chat-formatting rule for the three-line header (headline / issue / PR), the Unicode emoji set, and <…> URL wrapping so Discord does not stack preview cards. Run the prose through bench:deslop. If the reader is non-technical, use bench:chat-nontechnical.

Per execution-style and bench:refactor-flow: a refactor branch comes from the BASE branch (dev / master / main), never from a feature branch. Invoke bench:refactor-flow to sequence the merge into dependent feature branches afterwards.

Use the bench:deploy-status skill — it resolves the project's deploy config from projects.<key> and reports VM/container state, the live commit, /api/health and recent errors. Do not hand-roll gcloud calls; if auth fails, bench:gcloud-auth re-authenticates in the right Chrome profile.
